subject: biology
title: Root hair cells, xylem and phloem
key_idea: Root hair cells take in water by osmosis and mineral ions by active transport. Xylem carries water and mineral ions up from the roots. Phloem carries dissolved sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant. Each is adapted to its job.

blocks.text: Root hair cells are in the roots. They take in water and mineral ions from the soil.

items.meaning: The movement of water across a partially permeable membrane.
Moving substances against a concentration gradient, using energy from respiration.

items: Water is taken in by **osmosis**.
Mineral ions (such as nitrate) are taken in by **active transport**, from a low concentration in the soil to a higher concentration in the cell.
A long, thin projection gives a large surface area for absorption.
A thin cell wall means the water and mineral ions have a short distance to travel.
Many mitochondria release energy for active transport.
No chloroplasts: roots grow underground where there is no light, so they cannot photosynthesise.
Water enters root hair cells by osmosis. Mineral ions enter by active transport.
A large surface area increases the rate of absorption.
Active transport needs energy from many mitochondria.

blocks.text: Xylem and phloem are the plant's transport tissues. They run through the roots, stem and leaves.

items: Xylem
Phloem

values: Upwards: roots to stem and leaves
Up and down: from the leaves to the rest of the plant
Hollow tubes strengthened with lignin, no end walls
Tubes of elongated cells with pores in the end walls

items: Hollow tubes, with no cytoplasm and no end walls, so there is no obstruction and water flows easily.
Walls strengthened with **lignin**, to hold the tubes open.
Made of dead cells.

blocks.text: How water moves up the xylem

items: Water enters the root hair cells and passes into the xylem.
It travels up the xylem to the leaves.
It evaporates and leaves the leaf through the stomata. This movement is the **transpiration stream**.
Tubes of elongated living cells.
Pores in the end walls, so cell sap can move from one cell to the next.
Sugars are made in the leaves. They move up and down so every cell can respire and the meristems can grow.
Sugars can also be stored as starch, fat or oil.

diagram.alt: Sort each statement into xylem, phloem or both.

items.text: Made of dead cells with lignin
Moves substances up and down the plant
Found in roots, stems and leaves

items: Xylem: dead, hollow tubes with lignin. It carries water and mineral ions upwards.
Phloem: living cells with pores in the end walls. It carries dissolved sugars up and down.
If roots are damaged, less water and fewer mineral ions are absorbed, so photosynthesis and growth fall.

checks.q: Give two ways a root hair cell is adapted to absorb water and mineral ions.
checks.a: Any two from: long, thin projection giving a large surface area; thin cell wall so a short distance to travel; many mitochondria to release energy for active transport.

checks.q: Explain one way that xylem is adapted for its function.
checks.a: It is made of hollow tubes, so there is no obstruction to water flow. Or it has lignin, to hold the tubes open.

checks.q: Describe two differences between xylem and phloem.
checks.a: Any two from: xylem transports water and mineral ions but phloem transports dissolved sugars; xylem is dead cells but phloem is living cells; xylem moves substances upwards but phloem moves them up and down; phloem has pores in its end walls but xylem does not.

worked_example.question: Compare the structure and function of xylem tissue and phloem tissue.
answer_points: Structure: xylem is made of dead cells and phloem is made of living cells.
Structure: phloem cells have pores in their end walls. Xylem cells do not.
Structure: xylem is hollow, with no cytoplasm. Phloem contains cytoplasm.
Structure: xylem contains lignin. Phloem does not.
Structure: both are made of cells and both are tubular.
Function: xylem transports water and mineral ions. Phloem transports dissolved sugars.
Function: xylem is involved in transpiration and phloem in translocation.
Function: xylem transports in one direction (upwards). Phloem transports in both directions.
Function: both transport liquids throughout the plant.
worked_example.tip: For the top level you must refer to both structure and function, and make clear how they are similar or different.

worked_example.question: Sunflower plants grew and flowered. Explain how water moves through the stem of the sunflower plant to the leaves.
answer_points: Water travels through the xylem, from the root to the leaf.
With lignified walls, or walls made of dead cells.
Water is evaporated or diffused through the stomata.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score one mark each. Phloem carrying water is rejected.

items: Phloem is made of living cells.
Sucrose moves into and out of the phloem by active transport, which uses energy.
Water moves into and out of the xylem by osmosis.

worked_example.question: A gardener digs up a bush and then plants it in a different position in their garden. They try to dig up the bush with as much soil as possible so that the root hairs are not damaged. Explain why the gardener tries to prevent the root hairs being damaged.
answer_points: The plant might wilt, grow slower or photosynthesise less.
worked_example.tip: "Plant survival" is ignored. Give the effect on the plant.
